events.title: Krakatoa Reaches Its Climactic Eruption
events.description: The Krakatoa volcano in the Dutch East Indies (modern Indonesia) erupted in a series of massive explosions on August 26-27, with the most powerful blasts occurring on the morning of August 27. The explosions were heard thousands of kilometers away, and the resulting tsunamis devastated coastal communities in the Sunda Strait.
events.significance: The eruption killed an estimated 36,000 people, affected global weather and temperatures for years, produced vivid sunsets worldwide, and became one of the first major disasters reported around the world by telegraph.

events.title: Kellogg-Briand Pact Signed in Paris
events.description: Fifteen nations, including the United States, France, Germany, the United Kingdom, and Japan, signed the Kellogg-Briand Pact, formally renouncing war as an instrument of national policy. Many more countries later joined.
events.significance: Although it failed to prevent World War II, the pact established a foundation for the later legal prohibition of aggressive war and influenced the Nuremberg Trials and the UN Charter.

events.title: Birth of Lyndon B. Johnson
events.description: Lyndon Baines Johnson, the 36th President of the United States, was born near Stonewall, Texas. He became president in 1963 after the assassination of John F. Kennedy.
events.significance: Johnson championed the Great Society programs and signed the Civil Rights Act of 1964, the Voting Rights Act of 1965, and Medicare and Medicaid into law, while his escalation of the Vietnam War defined his troubled legacy.

events.title: Lord Mountbatten Assassinated by the IRA
events.description: Louis Mountbatten, 1st Earl Mountbatten of Burma, was killed when the Provisional IRA detonated a bomb on his fishing boat off the coast of Mullaghmore, County Sligo, Ireland. Three others on the boat also died, and the same day an IRA ambush at Warrenpoint killed 18 British soldiers.
events.significance: The attacks were among the deadliest of the Troubles, shocked Britain and Ireland, and intensified security cooperation and political debate over Northern Ireland.

events.title: Drake Well Strikes Oil in Pennsylvania
events.description: Edwin Drake's well near Titusville, Pennsylvania struck oil at a depth of about 69 feet, which is widely regarded as the beginning of the modern petroleum industry.
events.significance: The success of drilling for oil rather than collecting surface seepage launched a global industry that reshaped energy, transportation, economies, and geopolitics.
